brief: Morgan Stanley (Michael Wilson team) frames current conditions as a classic mid-cycle transition. More than 40% of Russell 3000 stocks have fallen 20%+ since June and the S&P 500 forward P/E compressed to 19x, matching the March lows, but median stock EPS growth in the mid-teens and revisions breadth near cycle highs have offset that valuation damage, containing index-level declines. The Fed hike under Chair Warsh is read as credibility-enhancing: with a hike already ~90% priced, the real signal was Warsh following through on his inflation-fighting stance, which MS argues can lower inflation uncertainty and term premium without necessarily raising long-term financing costs. August core CPI beat expectations but internals (soft shelter, fading tariff pass-through) were not uniformly hot. The bigger unresolved risk, in MS's view, is Warsh's monetarist approach to the Fed's balance sheet, not the 25bp hike itself. MS keeps large-cap quality (FCF yield, low accruals, AI-adopter margin gains) as its preferred positioning, citing prime brokerage flows confirming the rotation. It maintains its 8,000 year-end S&P 500 target, viewing 7000-7100 as a tactical downside case over the next 3-5 weeks if oil rises further or mid-term election seasonality (historically a 5-10% correction) bites, without abandoning the year-end target. A 10Y yield breach above 4.50% remains the key multiple-compression trigger.
